jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Serbia steers AI through Government strategies and non-binding ethics guidance. The AI Development Strategy 2025-2030, adopted in January 2025, replaced the 2020-2025 strategy and announces a dedicated AI law; the Government adopted ethics guidelines for reliable and responsible AI in 2023. The only binding rule is article 38 of the GDPR-aligned Law on Personal Data Protection, which covers decisions made solely by automated processing. No AI law or draft was found. Serbia is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).
lead_institutions: Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the ministry's, the national AI platform's, the Government's and the data protection commissioner's websites. The official gazette's search needs JavaScript and could not be used, and the review hit a search limit before the central bank, sector regulators and several ministries could be checked. The planned AI law and the 2025-2030 action plan are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia for the period 2025-2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Serbia (prepared on the initiative of the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Government on 10 January 2025 (05 Broj: 011-13287/2024-2, signed by Prime Minister Miloš Vučević); the final provisions order publication in the Službeni glasnik RS, but the gazette issue number could not be confirmed (the legislation portal is a JavaScript application not readable by the tools used). On entry into force it repealed the 2020-2025 strategy (Sl. glasnik RS 96/19). It provides that an action plan for 2025-2030 is adopted within 90 days and that implementation follows three-year action plans; no adopted action plan was found (see leads). Published on the ministry's Strategies page.
instruments.summary: Serbia's second national AI strategy, adopted under the Law on the Planning System, setting objectives and measures to 2030. It aims at a clear institutional and legal framework through a dedicated law regulating the application of AI aligned with international standards, AI education at all levels, support for research and innovation, AI use in the public and private sectors (medicine, biotechnology, education, agriculture, information security) and data governance and open data. It repeals the 2020-2025 strategy; under it, AI training programmes are approved by an AI Council and then accredited or certified.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; announces a dedicated AI law.

instruments.summary: Serbia's first national AI strategy, setting goals and measures so that AI drives economic growth, better public services, scientific capacity and future-oriented skills. It covers five areas: education, science and innovation, an AI-based economy, public-sector services using AI, and the ethical and safe application of AI in line with internationally recognised principles and the EU approach. Public administration, health and transport are named as priority public-sector domains.

instruments.current_status: Adopted by Government conclusion on 23 March 2023 (Government of Serbia statement of that date). The National AI Platform hosts a page for the guidelines and a companion self-assessment questionnaire ('Upitnik za proveru ispunjenosti uslova iz Etičkih smernica'), but both pages rendered without the document on 2026-10-13. instruments.summary: Government guidelines setting ethical principles and conditions for developing, deploying and using reliable and responsible AI in Serbia. Per the Government's adoption statement, they introduce a preventive mechanism so that machine-learning systems can be verified as meeting high ethical and security standards; a self-assessment questionnaire for meeting their conditions accompanies them on the National AI Platform.

instruments.official_title: Закон о заштити података о личности
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the National Assembly on 9 November 2018, promulgated 13 November 2018, published in Službeni glasnik RS 87/2018 (gazette issue date not printed in the copy read, hence YYYY-MM). Art. 102: in force on the eighth day after publication (21 November 2018 per the Commissioner's page) and applies nine months after entry into force (computed 21 August 2019), except art. 98. Copy read is the gazette text hosted by the Supreme Court; the Commissioner's page links a copy that returned HTTP 404. A Ministry working group on amendments exists (see leads).
instruments.summary: Serbia's GDPR-aligned general data protection law governing processing of personal data, including for AI training and use, enforced by the Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection. Art. 38 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal effects or significantly affect them, with exceptions (contract, law with safeguards, explicit consent) and minimum safeguards of human involvement, the right to express a view and to contest the decision; arts. 23-24 require information about such automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding national rule on automated decision-making/profiling.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full law text read (pdftotext) from the Supreme Court-hosted gazette copy; arts. 38 and 102 checked; Commissioner page read for adoption and entry-into-force dates.
